profileText: a Delegate from Virginia; born in Williamsburg, Va., August 10, 1753; graduated from the College of William and Mary, Williamsburg, Va.; studied law; admitted to the bar and commenced practice in Williamsburg; served in the Revolutionary War and was aide-de-camp to General Washington in the Continental Army; attorney general of Virginia, 1776; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1779; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1781 and 1782; elected governor of Virginia in 1786, but resigned in 1788, to serve in the Virginia state house of delegates in order that he might participate in the codification of the laws of Virginia in 1788 and 1789; delegate to the Federal Constitutional Convention in 1787; appointed the first Attorney General of the United States, in the Cabinet of President George Washington, on September 26, 1789; transferred to the State Department as Secretary of State on January 2, 1794, and served until August 19, 1795, when he was requested to resign following charges (subsequently found to be false) preferred by Minister Fauchet of France; was the principal counsel for Aaron Burr when the latter was tried for treason; died in Clarke County, Va., September 12, 1813; interment in the Old Chapel Cemetery, Millwood, Va.
